records.source: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לְאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ בֶּן־אֵלָ֧ה בְשֹׁמְר֛וֹן עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תֵּ֥שַׁע שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: In year two ten of Ahaz king of Judah reigned Hoshea son of Elah in Samaria over Israel nine years.
pieces: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned nine years.

L.1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah reigned in Samaria over Israel, nine years.

R.1: Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in the twelfth year that Ahaz was king of Judah. Hoshea ruled in Samaria for nine years.

decisions.choice: Hoshea son of Elah: the last king of Israel
decisions.reason: Hoshea took the throne by killing Pekah (15:30). His nine years end with the fall of Samaria and the end of the northern kingdom (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the twelfth year of Ahaz: one of several ways of counting the reigns
decisions.reason: 15:30 dates Hoshea's coup to the twentieth year of Jotham, Ahaz's father. The two dates do not fit together simply. Reigns in Kings sometimes overlapped, as when a son ruled beside his father, and were counted in more than one way, so the figures cannot always be lined up without remainder.

decisions.choice: reigned (Literal); became king ... and he reigned (Balanced); became king ... ruled (Readable)
decisions.reason: The accession formula has one wording at each level throughout Kings (1 Kings 16:8). Literal follows the Hebrew; Readable splits it into two sentences.

records.heading: Hoshea, the last king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה רַ֗ק לֹ֚א כְּמַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, only not like [the] kings of Israel who were before him.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, yet not as the kings of Israel before him had done.

L.2: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, only not like the kings of Israel who were before him.

R.2: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, but he was not as bad as the kings of Israel before him.

decisions.choice: only not like the kings before him: a lighter verdict, not explained
decisions.reason: Hoshea receives the evil verdict, but with a limit. Unlike nearly every king of Israel, he is not said to walk in the sin of Jeroboam. The writer does not say why. Hosea 10:5-6 speaks of the calf of Bethel being carried off to Assyria, and some think the calf worship had already been weakened; this cannot be shown from Kings.

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh: the verdict formula
decisions.reason: The standing verdict on a king in Kings (1 Kings 15:26, 34). Even the least bad of Israel's kings is judged by it, and the end of the kingdom comes in his reign: the fall is the result of the whole history the writer will now explain (verses 7-23).

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded the same way at each level throughout Kings.

decisions.choice: he was not as bad as
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "not like" means here: his evil was less than theirs.

records.source: עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה שַׁלְמַנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ֙ עֶ֔בֶד וַיָּ֥שֶׁב ל֖וֹ מִנְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria, and became to him Hoshea servant and returned to him tribute.
pieces: Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

L.3: Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria, and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.

R.3: Shalmaneser, the king of Assyria, marched against Hoshea. Hoshea had to submit to him and pay him tribute.

decisions.choice: Shalmaneser king of Assyria: Shalmaneser V
decisions.reason: Shalmaneser V succeeded his father Tiglath-pileser III (16:7-10) and reigned about 727-722 BC. Assyria was then the great power of the Near East.

decisions.choice: servant: a vassal, a subject king
decisions.reason: Here the word for a servant names a king bound by treaty to a greater king, who kept his throne as long as he stayed loyal and paid tribute (16:7; 24:1).

decisions.choice: returned to him tribute: paid him tribute
decisions.reason: "Returned" here means paid back what was owed. The word for tribute is the word for a gift or offering, used of the yearly payment a vassal owed his overlord (verse 4; 1 Kings 5:1).

decisions.choice: servant (Literal); vassal (Balanced); had to submit to him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servant" rather than "slave" because the word names a king's political subject, as it does for a king's officials. Balanced uses the exact term for a subject king; Readable describes it.

records.source: וַיִּמְצָא֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֨וּר בְּהוֹשֵׁ֜עַ קֶ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ אֶל־ס֣וֹא מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְלֹא־הֶעֱלָ֥ה מִנְחָ֛ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר כְּשָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֑ה וַֽיַּעַצְרֵ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא׃
records.gloss: And found [the] king of Assyria in Hoshea conspiracy, that he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and not brought up tribute to [the] king of Assyria as year by year; and shut him up [the] king of Assyria and bound him [in a] house of prison.
pieces: But the king of Assyria found Hoshea plotting against him, for he had sent envoys to So king of Egypt and had not paid the king of Assyria his tribute as in other years. So the king of Assyria arrested him and held him bound in prison.

L.4: And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and he had not brought up tribute to the king of Assyria as [he did] year by year. And the king of Assyria shut him up and bound him in a house of prison.

R.4: But the king of Assyria found out that Hoshea was plotting against him. Hoshea had sent messengers to So, the king of Egypt, and he had stopped paying the tribute he had paid the king of Assyria every year. So the king of Assyria arrested Hoshea and put him in prison in chains.

decisions.choice: So king of Egypt: an Egyptian ruler not yet clearly identified
alternatives: to Sais, to the king of Egypt
decisions.reason: No king of Egypt named So is known from Egyptian records. Egypt was then divided among several rulers. So may be a short form of the name of one of them, perhaps Osorkon IV, who ruled in the eastern Delta. Others read the Hebrew letters as the city of Sais, the seat of another ruler: "to Sais, to the king of Egypt". The Hebrew text as it stands reads a personal name.

decisions.choice: conspiracy: rebellion against his overlord
decisions.reason: The word is used for a plot against a king (1 Kings 15:27; 16:20). Here it is a vassal's breaking of his treaty: he sought help from Egypt and stopped paying.

decisions.choice: as year by year: as he had done every year before
decisions.reason: The tribute had been paid yearly; Hoshea now held it back.

decisions.choice: shut him up and bound him: Hoshea was taken before the siege
decisions.reason: Hoshea is in prison before the account of the siege (verse 5) and is not named at the fall of the city. He was probably seized when he came to his overlord, or captured outside the city, and Samaria held out without its king. Verses 5-6 then tell the campaign from its start.

decisions.choice: envoys
decisions.reason: Messengers sent from one king to another are envoys, a word that shows their official errand.

decisions.choice: he had stopped paying the tribute he had paid ... every year
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "as year by year" means (m3).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶ֖יהָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And came up [the] king of Assyria in all the land, and went up [to] Samaria and besieged it three years.
pieces: Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land. He went up to Samaria and laid siege to it for three years.

L.5: And the king of Assyria came up into all the land, and he went up to Samaria and besieged it three years.

R.5: Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole country. He came to Samaria and surrounded the city with his army for three years.

decisions.choice: three years: counted inclusively
decisions.reason: 18:9-10 dates the siege from Hoshea's seventh year to his ninth. Counting the first and last years in full, as Kings does, this is three years, though the siege itself may have lasted a little over two.

decisions.choice: came up ... went up: the invasion and then the siege
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: first of Assyria's army moving into the land, then of its march up the hill on which Samaria stood (1 Kings 16:24).

decisions.choice: surrounded the city with his army
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a siege is.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לָכַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ אֶת־שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַשּׁ֑וּרָה וַיֹּ֨שֶׁב אֹתָ֜ם בַּחְלַ֧ח וּבְחָב֛וֹר נְהַ֥ר גּוֹזָ֖ן וְעָרֵ֥י מָדָֽי׃פ
records.gloss: In year the ninth of Hoshea captured [the] king of Assyria Samaria, and exiled Israel to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and on Habor, river of Gozan, and [in the] cities of Media.
pieces: In Hoshea's ninth year the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried the Israelites away into exile to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, on the Habor, Gozan's river, and in the cities of the Medes.

L.6: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria, and he exiled Israel to Assyria, and he settled them in Halah and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and [in the] cities of the Medes.

R.6: In the ninth year that Hoshea was king, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. He took the people of Israel away to Assyria as captives. He made them live in Halah, by the Habor River in the region of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria captured Samaria: the end of the northern kingdom, about 722 BC
decisions.reason: The writer does not name the king. Shalmaneser V died about the time the city fell, and his successor Sargon II claims in his own inscriptions to have taken Samaria and deported its people. The kingdom of Israel, which had stood about two hundred years since the division (1 Kings 12), ended here.

decisions.choice: exiled: carried the people away from their land
decisions.reason: The verb means to remove a people into exile. Assyria moved conquered peoples to distant parts of its empire and brought others in to replace them (verse 24), so that they could not easily rebel. The same verb was used of the nations Yahweh removed before Israel (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Halah, the Habor, the river of Gozan, the cities of the Medes
decisions.reason: Halah lay in Assyria, north and east of Nineveh. The Habor is a river of upper Mesopotamia that flows south into the Euphrates; Gozan was a city and district on it. Media lay further east, in the mountains of what is now Iran, which Assyria had brought under its rule. The same list appears in 18:11.

decisions.choice: the Israelites (Balanced); the people of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Israel" here is the people, not the land or the kingdom, so Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: by the Habor River in the region of Gozan
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the Habor is the river and Gozan the district on it.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי־חָטְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם הַמַּעֲלֶ֤ה אֹתָם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִתַּ֕חַת יַ֖ד פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was because sinned [the] sons of Israel against Yahweh their God, who brought up them from [the] land of Egypt, from under [the] hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
pieces: This happened because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who had brought them up from the land of Egypt and out from under the power of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They had feared other gods.

L.7: And it was so because the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who had brought them up from the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they had feared other gods.

R.7: All this happened because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. He had brought them out of Egypt and freed them from the power of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. But they worshiped other gods.

decisions.choice: and it was because: the start of the writer's explanation
decisions.reason: Here the account turns from what happened to why it happened. Verses 7-23 look back over Israel's whole history and give the reason for the fall: not Assyria's strength but Israel's sin against its God.

decisions.choice: who brought them up from Egypt: the ground of the covenant
decisions.reason: The first of the Ten Commandments begins with the same act: "I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt", and goes on, "You shall have no other gods before me" (Exodus 20:2-3). The sin is ingratitude to the God who freed them.

decisions.choice: feared other gods: revered and worshiped them
decisions.reason: To fear a god is to stand in awe of him and worship him. The word runs through this chapter: Israel feared other gods (verses 7, 35, 37, 38), and the new settlers feared Yahweh and their own gods together (verses 32-33, 41).

decisions.choice: feared (Literal, Balanced); worshiped (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "feared" here (m3). Literal and Balanced keep "feared" so the chapter's repeated word stays visible (verses 25-41).

decisions.choice: the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control, as often.

records.heading: Why Israel went into exile

records.source: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ בְּחֻקּ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: And they walked in [the] statutes of the nations whom drove out Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel, and [of the] kings of Israel which they made.
pieces: They walked in the statutes of the nations whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and in the statutes that the kings of Israel had made.

L.8: And they walked in the statutes of the nations whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and [in those] of the kings of Israel, which they made.

R.8: They lived by the laws of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out of the land ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They also followed the laws that the kings of Israel had made.

decisions.choice: the statutes of the nations: the customs the nations lived by, above all in worship
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Yahweh's statutes (verses 13, 15, 34, 37). Here it is set against them: Israel kept the nations' rules instead of its God's. Leviticus 18:3 and 20:23 forbid walking in the statutes of the nations of Canaan.

decisions.choice: and of the kings of Israel which they made: the practices the kings of Israel set up
alternatives: and [walked after] the kings of Israel whom they made
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief. It most likely means the statutes the kings of Israel made, such as Jeroboam's calves with their priests and feasts (1 Kings 12:28-33; verses 21-22). It can also be read "and the kings of Israel whom they made", that is, the kings Israel set up for itself (Hosea 8:4).

decisions.choice: whom Yahweh had driven out: Israel copied the nations that lost the land
decisions.reason: The nations were driven out for these practices (Leviticus 18:24-28). By copying them, Israel brought the same end on itself.

decisions.choice: statutes (Literal, Balanced); laws (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word in these books, kept here so the contrast with Yahweh's statutes later in the chapter is visible.

records.source: וַיְחַפְּא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל דְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־כֵ֔ן עַל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּבְנ֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם בָּמוֹת֙ בְּכָל־עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל נוֹצְרִ֖ים עַד־עִ֥יר מִבְצָֽר׃
records.gloss: And did secretly [the] sons of Israel things which [were] not right against Yahweh their God, and built for themselves high places in all their cities, from tower of watchmen to city fortified.
pieces: In secret the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did things against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God that were not right. They built high places for themselves in all their towns, from the watchtower to the fortified city.

L.9: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did secretly things that [were] not right against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from watchmen's tower to fortified city.

R.9: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} secretly did wrong things against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. They built hilltop shrines for themselves in all their towns, from the smallest lookout tower to the largest walled city.

decisions.choice: did secretly: the meaning of a rare verb
decisions.reason: This verb occurs only here. It is usually linked to a word meaning "to cover", so "did in secret" or "covered over": they hid their wrongdoing or dressed it up as the worship of Yahweh. Others take it as "did things against" or "spoke things against" Yahweh.

decisions.choice: from watchmen's tower to fortified city: everywhere
decisions.reason: The phrase runs from the smallest place where people lived, a lookout tower in the fields, to the largest walled town (18:8). There was no settlement without its shrine.

decisions.choice: high places: local shrines
decisions.reason: Shrines with altars, often on hills, where sacrifice was made outside the temple (1 Kings 3:2; 14:23).

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The Readable wording kept for high places in these books.

decisions.choice: the smallest ... the largest
decisions.reason: Readable adds "smallest" and "largest" so the point of the phrase is clear (m2).

records.source: וַיַּצִּ֧בוּ לָהֶ֛ם מַצֵּב֖וֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים עַ֚ל כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן׃
records.gloss: And set up for themselves standing stones and Asherah poles on every hill high and under every tree green.
pieces: They set up standing stones and Asherah poles for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

L.10: And they set up for themselves standing stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

R.10: They set up stone pillars and poles used to worship Asherah on every high hill and under every large, leafy tree.

decisions.choice: standing stones and Asherah poles: objects of Canaanite worship
decisions.reason: Standing stones were upright stones set up as sacred markers; Asherah poles were wooden poles or trees that stood for the goddess Asherah. The law ordered Israel to break down both (Exodus 34:13; Deuteronomy 16:21-22).

decisions.choice: on every high hill and under every leafy tree: the places where the nations worshiped
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:2 commands Israel to destroy the places where the nations served their gods, on the hills and under every leafy tree. Judah built such places (1 Kings 14:23), Ahaz worshiped there (16:4), and Israel did the same.

decisions.choice: leafy: green and flourishing
decisions.reason: The word describes a tree in full leaf, green and flourishing; it is worded as in 1 Kings 14:23 and 16:4. Such shady trees were favored places for worship of fertility gods.

decisions.choice: standing stones, Asherah poles (Literal, Balanced); stone pillars, poles used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in Samuel and Kings.

records.source: וַיְקַטְּרוּ־שָׁם֙ בְּכָל־בָּמ֔וֹת כַּגּוֹיִ֕ם אֲשֶׁר־הֶגְלָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ דְּבָרִ֣ים רָעִ֔ים לְהַכְעִ֖יס אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And burned incense there on all high places like the nations whom exiled Yahweh from before them, and did things evil to provoke Yahweh.
pieces: There on all the high places they burned incense, as the nations had done whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} carried away before them, and they did evil things that provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger.

L.11: And they burned incense there on all the high places, like the nations whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had carried away before them, and they did evil things to provoke {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger.

R.11: They burned incense at all the hilltop shrines, as the nations had done before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} removed them from the land. They did evil things that made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry.

decisions.choice: burned incense: made offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke as an offering. It can refer to incense or to the burning of sacrifices; at the high places it probably covers both (1 Kings 3:3).

decisions.choice: whom Yahweh had carried away: removed from the land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Israel's exile in verse 6. The writer draws the parallel: the nations were removed for these practices, and now Israel has been removed for the same.

decisions.choice: to provoke to anger
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 16:2, the people's sin rouses Yahweh's anger (verse 17).

decisions.choice: carried away (Literal, Balanced); removed them from the land (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "take into exile"; here it is used of the nations driven out of Canaan, and "carried away" keeps the link to verse 6 without suggesting a deportation like Assyria's.

decisions.choice: provoke to anger (Literal, Balanced); made angry (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula as in 1 Kings 16:2.

records.source: וַיַּֽעַבְד֖וּ הַגִּלֻּלִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And they served the idols, which said Yahweh to them, Not you shall do the thing the this.
pieces: They served the idols, though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them, "You must not do this."

L.12: And they served the idols, of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to them, "You shall not do this thing."

R.12: They worshiped idols, even though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them, "Do not do this."

decisions.choice: the idols: a word of contempt for images of gods
decisions.reason: The word is used mostly in Ezekiel and in Kings of the idols of the nations and of Israel's kings (1 Kings 15:12; 21:26). It may come from a word for round lumps or for dung, and so mocks the idols as worthless things.

decisions.choice: you shall not do this thing: the commandment against idols
decisions.reason: The words sum up the commandments against making and serving images (Exodus 20:4-5; Deuteronomy 4:15-19).

decisions.choice: worshiped
decisions.reason: To serve a god means to worship it; Readable says so.

records.source: וַיָּ֣עַד יְהוָ֡ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וּבִיהוּדָ֡ה בְּיַד֩ כָּל־נְבִיאֵ֨י כָל־חֹזֶ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר שֻׁ֝֠בוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֤ם הָֽרָעִים֙ וְשִׁמְרוּ֙ מִצְוֺתַ֣י חֻקּוֹתַ֔י כְּכָ֨ל־הַתּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶת־אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדַ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃
records.gloss: And warned Yahweh Israel and Judah by [the] hand of every prophet [and] every seer, saying, Turn from your ways the evil, and keep my commandments, my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by [the] hand of my servants the prophets.
pieces: Yet {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer: "Turn back from your evil ways. Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, in keeping with the whole law that I commanded your ancestors and sent to you through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets."

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} warned Israel and Judah by the hand of every prophet [and] every seer, saying, "Turn from your evil ways and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, according to all the law that I commanded your fathers and that I sent to you by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves the prophets."

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer. He said, "Turn away from the evil things you are doing. Obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws. Follow all the teaching that I gave your ancestors and sent to you through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets."

decisions.choice: every prophet: reading the form noted in the margin of the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "his prophet", which does not fit the sentence. The Masoretes' marginal reading, followed here, gives "prophets of", so that the phrase means "all the prophets, every seer": every prophet Yahweh sent.

decisions.choice: warned: solemnly testified to them
decisions.reason: The verb means to call witnesses or to testify against someone, and so to warn with full solemnity (Deuteronomy 8:19; 30:19). It is the root of the word "testimonies" in verse 15: Yahweh's warnings were themselves part of his covenant.

decisions.choice: seer: another name for a prophet
decisions.reason: A seer is one who sees what Yahweh shows him in visions. The word is used alongside "prophet" for the same people (1 Samuel 9:9; 2 Samuel 24:11).

decisions.choice: turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments: the prophets' call
decisions.reason: This sums up the message of the prophets sent to Israel and Judah, from Ahijah and Elijah to Amos and Hosea: repent and return to the covenant. The law they called people back to was the one given to their ancestors at Sinai.

decisions.choice: commandments, statutes, law (Literal, Balanced); commands, laws, teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording settled for these terms (1 Kings 2:3).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The rule for this word: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable, as with "my servant David". The prophets belong wholly to Yahweh and act for him.

records.source: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּקְשׁ֤וּ אֶת־עָרְפָּם֙ כְּעֹ֣רֶף אֲבוֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א הֶאֱמִ֔ינוּ בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And not they listened, and stiffened their neck like [the] neck of their fathers, who not trusted in Yahweh their God.
pieces: But they would not listen. They stiffened their necks as their ancestors had done, who did not trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

L.14: And they did not listen, and they stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who did not trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

R.14: But they would not listen. They were stubborn, just like their ancestors, who did not trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: stiffened their neck: refused to obey
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that stiffens its neck against the yoke and will not be led. It is said of Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 32:9; Deuteronomy 9:6; 10:16; 31:27), and their descendants are like them.

decisions.choice: who did not trust in Yahweh: the wilderness generation
decisions.reason: The same words are used of the generation that refused to enter the land (Numbers 14:11; Deuteronomy 1:32; 9:23). To trust in Yahweh is to rely on him and take him at his word.

decisions.choice: were stubborn
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1), as in Deuteronomy 9:6. Literal and Balanced keep the picture.

records.source: וַיִּמְאֲס֣וּ אֶת־חֻקָּ֗יו וְאֶת־בְּרִיתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֣ת אֶת־אֲבוֹתָ֔ם וְאֵת֙ עֵֽדְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵעִ֖יד בָּ֑ם וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּאַחֲרֵ֤י הַהֶ֨בֶל֙ וַיֶּהְבָּ֔לוּ וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבִֽיבֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֖י עֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they rejected his statutes and his covenant which he made with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified against them; and they walked after the vanity and became vain, and after the nations which [were] around them, which commanded Yahweh them not to do like them.
pieces: They rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with their ancestors, and the decrees by which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had warned them. They went after worthless idols and became worthless themselves. They followed the nations around them, although {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded them not to do as those nations did.

L.15: And they rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with their fathers, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies with which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} warned them; and they went after worthless idols and became worthless, and after the nations that [were] around them, concerning whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded them not to do as they [did].

R.15: They rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws and the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with their ancestors. They ignored the instructions {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given to warn them. They followed useless idols and became useless themselves. They copied the nations around them, even though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded them not to live like those nations.

decisions.choice: the vanity: worthless idols
decisions.reason: The word *hevel* means a breath or vapor, something empty and passing. Used of gods it names idols as nothing at all (Deuteronomy 32:21; 1 Kings 16:13).

decisions.choice: went after worthless idols and became worthless: people become like what they worship
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from the same word: they followed *hevel* and became *hevel*. Jeremiah 2:5 says the same of Judah, and Psalm 115:8 says that those who make idols become like them.

decisions.choice: his testimonies with which he warned them: the covenant's solemn terms
decisions.reason: "Testimonies" and "warned" share a root (verse 13). The covenant terms were themselves a warning, declared before witnesses, of what would follow if the covenant was broken (Deuteronomy 31:26-29).

decisions.choice: they rejected his statutes and his covenant
decisions.reason: Israel's rejection of Yahweh comes first; his rejection of them follows (verse 20). The same verb is used both times.

decisions.choice: worthless idols ... became worthless (Literal, Balanced); useless idols ... became useless (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 16:13. Each level repeats one word so the play between noun and verb is kept (m2).

decisions.choice: statutes, testimonies (Literal); statutes, decrees (Balanced); laws, instructions (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these terms (1 Kings 2:3).

records.source: וַיַּעַזְב֗וּ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם מַסֵּכָ֖ה שְׁנֵ֣י עֲגָלִ֑ים וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֲשֵׁירָ֗ה וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לְכָל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־הַבָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: And they forsook all [the] commandments of Yahweh their God, and made for themselves a cast image, two calves, and made an Asherah pole, and bowed down to all [the] host of the heavens, and served the Baal.
pieces: They abandoned every commandment of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God and made themselves cast images, two calves. They made an Asherah pole, bowed down to all the host of heaven, and served Baal.

L.16: And they forsook all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and they made for themselves a cast image, two calves, and they made an Asherah pole, and they bowed down to all the host of the heavens, and they served the Baal.

R.16: They turned away from all the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. They made two metal statues of calves for themselves. They set up a pole used to worship Asherah. They bowed down to the sun, moon and stars, and they worshiped the god Baal.

decisions.choice: a cast image, two calves: Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: Jeroboam set up two golden calves, one at Bethel and one at Dan (1 Kings 12:28-29). The words recall the cast calf Israel made at Sinai (Exodus 32:4, 8): the northern kingdom began by repeating that sin.

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the sun, moon and stars worshiped as gods
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean Yahweh's heavenly court (1 Kings 22:19), but here it is the heavenly bodies, which the nations worshiped and the law forbade Israel to worship (Deuteronomy 4:19; 17:3). This worship grew under Assyrian influence (21:3-5; 23:4-5).

decisions.choice: an Asherah pole; the Baal
decisions.reason: Ahab made an Asherah pole and served Baal in Samaria (1 Kings 16:31-33). Jehu destroyed Baal's temple there (10:27-28), but the writer counts the whole history together.

decisions.choice: the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: Readable names what "the host of heaven" means here (m2), as in Deuteronomy 4:19.

decisions.choice: cast images (Balanced); metal statues (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew singular stands for the two calves together; Balanced uses the plural so the list reads naturally.

records.source: וַֽ֠יַּעֲבִירוּ אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֤ם וְאֶת־בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּקְסְמ֥וּ קְסָמִ֖ים וַיְנַחֵ֑שׁוּ וַיִּֽתְמַכְּר֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they made pass their sons and their daughters in the fire, and divined divinations and practiced omens, and sold themselves to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, to provoke him.
pieces: They made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, practiced divination and read omens, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.

L.17: And they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, and they practiced divination and read omens, and they sold themselves to do the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.

R.17: They burned their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices. They used magic to learn secret things and read signs to know the future. They gave themselves completely to doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, and this made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: made their sons and daughters pass through the fire: child sacrifice
decisions.reason: The law forbids it as the practice of the nations (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 18:10). Ahaz of Judah had done it (16:3), and Jeremiah 7:31 says plainly that children were burned. Some think the phrase could also cover a rite of passing children through fire to dedicate them, but in Kings it names the worst of the nations' practices.

decisions.choice: practiced divination and read omens: seeking hidden knowledge
decisions.reason: Two kinds of fortune-telling forbidden together in Deuteronomy 18:10: the first, consulting spirits or casting lots for an answer; the second, reading signs and omens.

decisions.choice: sold themselves: gave themselves over wholly
decisions.reason: Like someone who sells himself as a slave, they handed themselves over to doing evil. The same is said of Ahab (1 Kings 21:20, 25).

decisions.choice: burned ... as sacrifices; used magic to learn secret things; read signs to know the future
decisions.reason: Readable explains these practices in plain words, as in Deuteronomy 18:10.

decisions.choice: the verdict formula
decisions.reason: Worded as in verse 2.

records.source: וַיִּתְאַנַּ֨ף יְהוָ֤ה מְאֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְסִרֵ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו לֹ֣א נִשְׁאַ֔ר רַ֛ק שֵׁ֥בֶט יְהוּדָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And was angry Yahweh very with Israel, and removed them from before his face; not was left [any] only [the] tribe of Judah by itself.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with Israel and removed them from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. None was left but the tribe of Judah alone.

L.18: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} removed them from before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face; none was left except the tribe of Judah alone.

R.18: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. Only the tribe of Judah was left.

decisions.choice: removed them from before his face: sent them away from his presence
decisions.reason: To be before Yahweh's face is to live in his land, under his care, where he is worshiped. Exile takes them out of it (verse 23; 13:23).

decisions.choice: the tribe of Judah alone: the southern kingdom
decisions.reason: Judah stands for the whole kingdom of the south, which included Benjamin (1 Kings 12:21). The prophet Ahijah had spoken of Judah as the one tribe left to David's house (1 Kings 11:32, 36).

decisions.choice: his presence
decisions.reason: "Face" stands for presence, as often.

records.source: גַּם־יְהוּדָ֕ה לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר אֶת־מִצְוֺ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ בְּחֻקּ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: Also Judah not kept [the] commandments of Yahweh their God, and they walked in [the] statutes of Israel which they made.
pieces: Even Judah failed to keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. They walked in the statutes that Israel had made.

L.19: Judah also did not keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and they walked in the statutes of Israel that they made.

R.19: But even the people of Judah did not obey the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. They followed the laws that Israel had made.

decisions.choice: Judah too: a look ahead to Judah's fall
decisions.reason: The writer breaks off to say that Judah, the tribe left in verse 18, was no better. Judah would later be exiled for the same reasons (21:10-15; 23:26-27; 24:3-4).

decisions.choice: the statutes of Israel which they made: the practices Israel introduced
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, the statutes are the customs of worship Israel and its kings set up. "They" most naturally refers to Israel; it could also mean Judah adopting them.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Judah is a people here, which fits the plural verb that follows.

records.source: וַיִּמְאַ֨ס יְהוָ֜ה בְּכָל־זֶ֤רַע יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיְעַנֵּ֔ם וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַד־שֹׁסִ֑ים עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁלִיכָ֖ם מִפָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And rejected Yahweh all [the] offspring of Israel, and afflicted them and gave them into [the] hand of plunderers, until that he cast them from his presence.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejected all Israel's descendants. He afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had thrown them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

L.20: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejected all the offspring of Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} afflicted them and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had cast them out from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

R.20: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejected all the descendants of Israel. He punished them and let raiders rob them, until at last {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} threw them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

decisions.choice: Yahweh rejected: the answer to Israel's rejection
decisions.reason: The same verb was used of Israel rejecting Yahweh's statutes and covenant (verse 15). What they did to him he now does to them.

decisions.choice: all the offspring of Israel: the whole people
decisions.reason: After verse 19 the phrase may take in Judah too, whose rejection the writer foresees. In this passage it most likely means the northern kingdom, whose fall is being explained (verses 18, 21-23).

decisions.choice: gave them into the hand of plunderers: as in the days of the judges
decisions.reason: The same words describe Yahweh's discipline in Judges 2:14. Before the end came, Israel suffered raids and losses that should have turned them back (13:3, 7; 15:29).

decisions.choice: let raiders rob them
decisions.reason: Readable puts the picture of plunderers into a plain sentence.

records.source: כִּֽי־קָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵעַל֙ בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד וַיַּמְלִ֖יכוּ אֶת־יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט וַיַּדַּ֨ח יָרָבְעָ֤ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְהֶחֱטֵיאָ֖םחֲטָאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: For he tore Israel from upon [the] house of David, and they made king Jeroboam son of Nebat; and drove away Jeroboam Israel from after Yahweh, and made them sin a sin great.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had torn Israel from David's house, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam drove Israel away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and led them to commit a great sin.

L.21: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tore Israel from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and made them sin a great sin.

R.21: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tore Israel away from David's family, the people made Jeroboam son of Nebat their king. Jeroboam drew Israel away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and led them into a great sin.

decisions.choice: he tore Israel from the house of David: Yahweh is the subject
alternatives: when Israel tore itself away from the house of David
decisions.reason: Yahweh, named in verse 20, tore the kingdom from David's house, as Ahijah said with the torn cloak (1 Kings 11:11, 31). The Hebrew can also be read with Israel as subject: "Israel tore itself away from the house of David" (compare 1 Kings 12:19).

decisions.choice: drove away: the reading of the Hebrew margin
decisions.reason: The written text and the Masoretes' marginal reading differ slightly in the form of this verb; both point to the verb meaning to drive away or lure away, used of leading people away from Yahweh in Deuteronomy 13:6, 11.

decisions.choice: made them sin a great sin: the sin of Jeroboam
decisions.reason: Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-30) are the sin by which he made Israel sin, the charge laid on nearly every king of Israel after him. "A great sin" is what Moses called the golden calf (Exodus 32:21, 30).

decisions.choice: made them sin (Literal); led them to commit (Balanced); led them into (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula of the sin of Jeroboam has one wording at each level in Kings (1 Kings 16:2). Balanced adds "commit" because the object "a great sin" follows.

decisions.choice: the LORD (for "he")
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, following m1.

records.source: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּכָל־חַטֹּ֥אות יָרָבְעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה לֹא־סָ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And walked [the] sons of Israel in all [the] sins of Jeroboam which he did; not they turned from it,
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} walked in all the sins that Jeroboam committed and did not turn away from them,

L.22: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam that he did; they did not turn aside from them,

R.22: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} kept on committing all the sins that Jeroboam had committed. They never turned away from them.

decisions.choice: from it: from the sin of Jeroboam
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from it", treating Jeroboam's sins as one: the worship he set up. The sentence runs on into verse 23.

decisions.choice: walked in all the sins of Jeroboam: the whole history of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: What was said of each king (1 Kings 15:26, 34; 16:26) is now said of the people as a whole: from Jeroboam to the end, they never left his way of worship.

decisions.choice: kept on committing
decisions.reason: Readable puts "walked in" as ongoing action, and ends the sentence here; verse 23 begins a new one.

records.source: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר־הֵסִ֨יר יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד כָּל־עֲבָדָ֣יו הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים וַיִּ֨גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתוֹ֙ אַשּׁ֔וּרָה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: until that removed Yahweh Israel from before his face, as he had spoken by [the] hand of all his servants the prophets; and went into exile Israel from upon its land to Assyria until the day the this.
pieces: until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} removed Israel from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said through all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets. So Israel went into exile from its own land to Assyria, to this day.

L.23: until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} removed Israel from before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken by the hand of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves the prophets. And Israel went into exile from its land to Assyria, to this day.

R.23: This went on until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Israel away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had warned through all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets. So the people of Israel were taken away from their own land as captives to Assyria, and they are still there to this day.

decisions.choice: as he had spoken through his servants the prophets
decisions.reason: Ahijah had foretold that Yahweh would uproot Israel and scatter it beyond the River for Jeroboam's sins (1 Kings 14:15-16), and Amos and Hosea warned of exile (Amos 5:27; 7:17; Hosea 9:3). Kings shows the prophets' word coming true.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As in 2:22, "to this day" means the time when the account was written. The exiles of the northern kingdom had not returned.

decisions.choice: went into exile: was carried away from its land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the deportation in verse 6. Verses 7-23 end where they began.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: This went on until ...; they are still there
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence, since verse 22 ended its own, and spells out what "to this day" means here.

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֡וּר מִבָּבֶ֡ל וּ֠מִכּוּ֠תָה וּמֵעַוָּ֤א וּמֵֽחֲמָת֙ וּסְפַרְוַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֨שֶׁב֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן תַּ֖חַת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽרְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֵּֽשְׁב֖וּ בְּעָרֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And brought [the] king of Assyria from Babylon and from Cuthah and from Avva and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and settled [them] in [the] cities of Samaria in place of [the] sons of Israel; and they took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
pieces: From Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim the king of Assyria brought people and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.

L.24: And the king of Assyria brought [people] from Babylon and from Cuthah and from Avva and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and he settled [them] in the cities of Samaria in place of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. And they took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.

R.24: The king of Assyria brought in people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim. He made them live in the towns of Samaria in place of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They took over Samaria and lived in its towns.

decisions.choice: brought ... and settled them: Assyria's exchange of peoples
decisions.reason: Assyria moved conquered peoples away and brought others from far parts of the empire in their place, so that no people could easily rebel in its own land. Sargon II records settling foreigners in Samaria, and later kings sent more (Ezra 4:2, 10).

decisions.choice: Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, Sepharvaim
decisions.reason: Babylon and Cuthah were cities of southern Mesopotamia, which Assyria then ruled. Hamath was a city of Syria on the Orontes river. Avva and Sepharvaim are not certainly located; they are named with Hamath again in 18:34 and 19:13, and were probably in Syria.

decisions.choice: Samaria: now the name of the region
decisions.reason: "The cities of Samaria" are the towns of the land around the capital. From here on Samaria names the whole province, not only the city.

decisions.choice: took possession of Samaria
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Israel taking possession of Canaan (Deuteronomy 1:8). Now others take possession of Israel's land, as the nations once lost it to Israel (verses 8, 11).

decisions.choice: took over
decisions.reason: Readable puts "took possession of" in plain words.

records.heading: New settlers in Samaria

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בִּתְחִלַּת֙ שִׁבְתָּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם לֹ֥א יָרְא֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֤ה בָּהֶם֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲרָי֔וֹת וַיִּֽהְי֥וּ הֹרְגִ֖ים בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] beginning of their living there, not they feared Yahweh, and sent Yahweh among them the lions, and they were killing among them.
pieces: When they first lived there they did not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.

L.25: And it was at the beginning of their living there [that] they did not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent the lions among them, and they were killing [some] among them.

R.25: When they first began living there, they did not worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of the people.

decisions.choice: fear Yahweh: revere and worship him
decisions.reason: To fear Yahweh is to hold him in awe and worship him as God. The word becomes the theme of verses 25-41: the settlers learn to "fear" Yahweh in their own way, but not as the covenant requires (verses 32-34, 41).

decisions.choice: Yahweh sent lions: the land is still his
decisions.reason: Israel has gone, but Yahweh has not given up his land. Lions lived in the thickets of the land (1 Kings 13:24; 20:36), and the law warned that wild animals would increase in a land left empty or in one that broke the covenant (Exodus 23:29; Leviticus 26:22).

decisions.choice: fear (Literal, Balanced); worship (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "fear", the word this section turns on, from here to verse 41. Readable says "worship", which is what the word means here (m1).

decisions.choice: some of them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the lions were killing "among them": not all, but some.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִגְלִ֨יתָ֙ וַתּ֨וֹשֶׁב֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיְשַׁלַּח־בָּ֣ם אֶת־הָאֲרָי֗וֹת וְהִנָּם֙ מְמִיתִ֣ים אוֹתָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ אֵינָ֣ם יֹדְעִ֔ים אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And they said to [the] king of Assyria, saying, The nations which you exiled and settled in [the] cities of Samaria not know [the] custom of [the] god of the land, and he sent among them the lions, and look, they [are] killing them, because they [are] not knowing [the] custom of [the] god of the land.
pieces: Word was brought to the king of Assyria: "The nations you carried away and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom of the god of the land. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent lions among them, and they are killing them, because they do not know what the god of the land requires."

L.26: And they said to the king of Assyria, "The nations that you exiled and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom of the god of the land, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent the lions among them, and look, they are killing them, because they do not know the custom of the god of the land."

R.26: Someone told the king of Assyria, "The people you moved into the towns of Samaria do not know how the god of that land must be worshiped. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent lions among them, and the lions are killing them. This is because the people do not know what the god of the land requires."

decisions.choice: the custom of the god of the land: the way he must be worshiped
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a ruling or judgment, but here it means the proper practice: the rites and rules by which a god expects to be served. The settlers think of Yahweh as a local god with his own customs, like the gods of their homelands.

decisions.choice: the god of the land: a god tied to a territory
decisions.reason: The peoples of the ancient Near East commonly held that each land had its own god, who had to be served there in the right way (1 Kings 20:23, 28). The speakers see Yahweh so; the writer knows him as the God of the whole earth.

decisions.choice: they said: an unnamed report
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. Someone, perhaps the settlers or Assyrian officials, reported to the king.

decisions.choice: custom (Literal); custom, what ... requires (Balanced); how ... must be worshiped, what ... requires (Readable)
decisions.reason: This word is usually "judgments" or "rulings" in a list of laws. Here it stands alone and means a custom of worship (m1), so each level says that.

decisions.choice: god (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The speakers mean the local god of Samaria; the lowercase word gives their view. The pronoun for him takes the reader's setting because the one who sent the lions is Yahweh (verse 25).

decisions.choice: Word was brought to (Balanced); Someone told (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the verb without a named subject a natural form (m3).

records.source: וַיְצַ֨ו מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֜וּר לֵאמֹ֗ר הֹלִ֤יכוּ שָׁ֨מָּה֙ אֶחָ֤ד מֵהַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִגְלִיתֶ֣ם מִשָּׁ֔ם וְיֵלְכ֖וּ וְיֵ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֑ם וְיֹרֵ֕ם אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And commanded [the] king of Assyria, saying, Take there one of the priests whom you exiled from there, and let them go and live there, and let him teach them [the] custom of [the] god of the land.
pieces: Then the king of Assyria gave orders: "Send back there one of the priests you carried away from there. Let him go and live there and teach them the custom of the god of the land."

L.27: And the king of Assyria commanded, saying, "Take there one of the priests whom you exiled from there, and let them go and live there, and let him teach them the custom of the god of the land."

R.27: So the king of Assyria gave an order: "Send back one of the priests you took away from there. Let him go and live there and teach the people how the god of that land must be worshiped."

decisions.choice: let them go and live there: a plural among singulars
alternatives: let them go and live there
decisions.reason: The verbs "go" and "live" are plural, though one priest is sent and "teach" is singular. The plural may include the priest's household or helpers, or the king may be speaking loosely; some ancient translations read the singular.

decisions.choice: teach them the custom of the god of the land
decisions.reason: The king treats the problem as a matter of ritual know-how: teach the right rites and the god will be satisfied. Verses 32-41 show that this does not bring the whole-hearted loyalty Yahweh asks.

decisions.choice: let him go (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the singular, since one priest is sent (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew plural.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֞א אֶחָ֣ד מֵהַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִגְלוּ֙ מִשֹּׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וַֽיְהִי֙ מוֹרֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם אֵ֖יךְ יִֽירְא֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And came one of the priests whom they exiled from Samaria and lived in Bethel, and he was teaching them how they should fear Yahweh.
pieces: So one of the priests who had been carried away from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and he taught them how they should fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: And one of the priests whom they had exiled from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and he was teaching them how they should fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: So one of the priests who had been taken away from Samaria came back and lived in Bethel. He taught the people how to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Bethel: the shrine of Jeroboam's calf
decisions.reason: Bethel was where Jeroboam set up one of his golden calves and its priests (1 Kings 12:29-33). The priest sent back was one of the northern kingdom's priests, and he taught the worship of Yahweh as it had been practiced there, the very worship this chapter condemns (verses 16, 21-22).

decisions.choice: teaching: instructing them
decisions.reason: The word is related to *torah*, "instruction, law". What he taught was how to fear Yahweh (verse 25), but the teaching produced a mixed worship (verses 32-33).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

records.source: וַיִּהְי֣וּ עֹשִׂ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיַּנִּ֣יחוּ׀בְּבֵ֣ית הַבָּמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרֹנִ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּוֹי֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And were making nation [by] nation its gods, and set [them] in [the] house of the high places which made the Samaritans, nation [by] nation in their cities where they [were] living there.
pieces: But each nation made its own gods and set them up in the shrines of the high places that the people of Samaria had made, each nation in the cities where it lived.

L.29: And each nation was making its own gods, and they set [them] in the house of the high places that the Samaritans had made, nation by nation, in their cities where they were living.

R.29: But each group of people made its own gods. They put them in the hilltop shrines that the people of Samaria had built. Each group did this in the towns where it lived.

decisions.choice: the Samaritans: the Israelites who had lived in Samaria
decisions.reason: This is the only place the word occurs in the Hebrew Bible. Here it means the former people of the kingdom of Samaria, who had built the high places, not the later community known by that name.

decisions.choice: the house of the high places: shrine buildings
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 12:31, the singular "house" stands for many shrine buildings at the high places. The newcomers reused Israel's own shrines for their gods.

decisions.choice: nation nation: each nation
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun means "each one": every people did this in its own towns.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The Readable wording for the high places.

records.source: וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בָבֶ֗ל עָשׂוּ֙ אֶת־סֻכּ֣וֹת בְּנ֔וֹת וְאַנְשֵׁי־כ֔וּת עָשׂ֖וּ אֶת־נֵֽרְגַ֑ל וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י חֲמָ֖ת עָשׂ֥וּ אֶת־אֲשִׁימָֽא׃
records.gloss: And [the] men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, and [the] men of Cuth made Nergal, and [the] men of Hamath made Ashima.
pieces: The {{gender:people|men}} of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the {{gender:people|men}} of Cuth made Nergal, and the {{gender:people|men}} of Hamath made Ashima.

L.30: And the {{gender:people|men}} of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, and the {{gender:people|men}} of Cuth made Nergal, and the {{gender:people|men}} of Hamath made Ashima.

R.30: The {{gender:people|men}} from Babylon made idols of Succoth-benoth. The {{gender:people|men}} from Cuth made idols of Nergal, and the {{gender:people|men}} from Hamath made idols of Ashima.

decisions.choice: Succoth-benoth, Nergal, Ashima: the settlers' gods
decisions.reason: Nergal was the Mesopotamian god of the underworld and of plague, worshiped above all at Cuth. Succoth-benoth and Ashima are not known for certain: the first may be a form of the name of a Babylonian god or goddess, the second a god or goddess of Hamath.

decisions.choice: made: made images of the gods and worshiped them
decisions.reason: To "make" a god is to make its image and set up its worship (verse 29).

decisions.choice: Cuth: the same city as Cuthah
decisions.reason: Verse 24 gives the name as Cuthah; this is a shorter form.

decisions.choice: made idols of
decisions.reason: Readable says what "made" means here (m2).

records.source: וְהָעַוִּ֛ים עָשׂ֥וּ נִבְחַ֖ז וְאֶת־תַּרְתָּ֑ק וְהַסְפַרְוִ֗ים שֹׂרְפִ֤ים אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ לְאַדְרַמֶּ֥לֶךְ וַֽעֲנַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֱלֹהֵ֥י סְפַרְוָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites [were] burning their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, [the] gods of Sepharvaim.
pieces: The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, while the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire for Adrammelech and Anammelech, gods of Sepharvaim.

L.31: And the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites were burning their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

R.31: The Avvites made idols of Nibhaz and Tartak. The people from Sepharvaim burned their children in the fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of their city.

decisions.choice: Nibhaz and Tartak: gods of Avva
decisions.reason: Neither god is known outside this verse.

decisions.choice: Adrammelech and Anammelech: gods honored with child sacrifice
decisions.reason: Both names end in a word meaning "king", like Molech, to whom children were burned (Leviticus 18:21). The settlers brought into the land the very practice for which Israel was condemned (verse 17).

decisions.choice: the gods of Sepharvaim: the marginal reading
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells these two words differently from the reading given in the margin; the marginal reading, "the gods of Sepharvaim", is followed, and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: made idols of; as sacrifices; their city
decisions.reason: Readable explains "made" (verse 30) and the burning, and names Sepharvaim as the settlers' home city.

records.source: וַיִּהְי֥וּ יְרֵאִ֖ים אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם מִקְצוֹתָם֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י בָמ֔וֹת וַיִּהְי֛וּ עֹשִׂ֥ים לָהֶ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית הַבָּמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And they were fearing Yahweh, and made for themselves from [the] whole range of themselves priests of high places, and they were offering for them in [the] house of the high places.
pieces: They feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but they also appointed priests of the high places from all sorts of their own people, who offered sacrifices for them in the shrines of the high places.

L.32: And they were fearing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they made for themselves priests of high places from the whole range of themselves, and they were offering for them in the house of the high places.

R.32: They worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but they also chose priests for the hilltop shrines from all kinds of people among them. These priests offered sacrifices for them in the shrines.

decisions.choice: from the whole range of themselves: from anyone among them
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of Jeroboam's priests (1 Kings 12:31): priests chosen from any family, not from the tribe of Levi. The settlers repeat Jeroboam's practice.

decisions.choice: they feared Yahweh, and made priests of high places
decisions.reason: The two halves stand side by side without comment. The settlers added Yahweh to their worship but kept the high places and priests the law forbade.

decisions.choice: but they also
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the clauses with "and"; Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast the next verse makes plain.

decisions.choice: fearing (Literal); feared (Balanced); worshiped (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

records.source: אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה הָי֣וּ יְרֵאִ֑ים וְאֶת־אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ הָי֣וּ עֹֽבְדִ֔ים כְּמִשְׁפַּט֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הִגְל֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם מִשָּֽׁם׃
records.gloss: Yahweh they were fearing, and their gods they were serving, according to [the] custom of the nations whom they exiled them from there.
pieces: They feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they served their own gods, according to the custom of the nations from which they had been carried away.

L.33: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} they were fearing, and their own gods they were serving, according to the custom of the nations from which they had exiled them.

R.33: They worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but they also served their own gods, just as the nations they had been taken from did.

decisions.choice: they feared Yahweh and served their own gods: divided worship
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts each object first: "Yahweh they feared, and their gods they served." It sums up verses 24-32. Yahweh asked for the whole of his people's worship (verses 35-36); a share alongside other gods was not the fear he required (verse 34).

decisions.choice: the custom of the nations: the religious practice of their homelands
decisions.reason: As in verse 26, the word means custom. They worshiped as people did in the lands they came from.

decisions.choice: from which they had exiled them: from which the Assyrians had deported them
decisions.reason: "They" here are the Assyrians, an unnamed subject; the settlers are the ones exiled.

decisions.choice: Yahweh they were fearing, and their own gods they were serving
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which sets the two objects side by side (m1).

decisions.choice: had been carried away (Balanced); had been taken from (Readable)

pieces: To this day they keep to their former customs. They do not truly fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they do not follow their statutes and rulings, or the law and the commandment that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the descendants of Jacob, the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Israel.

L.34: To this day they are doing according to the former customs. They do not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they do not do according to their statutes and according to their judgment, or according to the law and according to the commandment that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded the {{gender:children|sons}} of Jacob, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Israel.

R.34: To this day they still follow their old customs. They do not really worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They do not obey the laws and rules, the teaching and the commands that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to the descendants of Jacob, the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Israel.

decisions.choice: they do not fear Yahweh: not the fear the covenant asks
decisions.reason: Verse 33 said they feared Yahweh; this verse says they do not. Both are true from different sides: they gave Yahweh a place among their gods, but fearing him as the covenant means it is to serve him alone (verses 35-39). A share is no fear at all.

decisions.choice: they ... their statutes: who is meant
decisions.reason: "They" are most naturally the people of the land in the writer's day, settlers and remaining Israelites together. "Their statutes and their judgment" are then the statutes that belonged to the land's people, the ones Yahweh gave Israel. Some take verses 34-40 to speak of the exiled Israelites instead.

decisions.choice: the sons of Jacob, whom he named Israel
decisions.reason: God gave Jacob the name Israel (Genesis 32:29; 35:10), and Elijah recalled it at Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:31). The covenant was made with Jacob's descendants, not with the nations now in the land.

decisions.choice: customs; statutes, judgment, law, commandment
decisions.reason: The first word is the one used for custom in verses 26 and 33. In the list that follows it is one of four terms for what Yahweh commanded, as in 1 Kings 2:3.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgment, law, commandment / statutes, rulings, law, commandment / laws, rules, teaching, commands
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these terms (1 Kings 2:3). The first word in the verse is "customs" at every level, as in verse 33.

decisions.choice: truly (Balanced); really (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add a word so that "do not fear" does not seem to contradict verse 33 (m1).

decisions.choice: you shall not fear other gods, nor bow down to them, nor serve them
decisions.reason: The words come from the first two commandments (Exodus 20:3-5; Deuteronomy 5:7-9) and from Deuteronomy 6:13-14. Verses 35-39 sum up the covenant in Yahweh's own words, repeating "do not fear other gods" three times (verses 35, 37, 38).

decisions.choice: with them: with the descendants of Jacob
decisions.reason: "Them" refers back to the sons of Jacob in verse 34: the covenant at Sinai, made with Israel.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

pieces: but fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm. Bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and sacrifice to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.36: but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall fear, and to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall bow down, and to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall sacrifice.

decisions.choice: with an outstretched arm: with mighty power
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength in action. The phrase is used of the exodus in Deuteronomy (4:34; 5:15; 26:8).

decisions.choice: but only Yahweh ... him you shall fear
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Yahweh first and repeats "him" with each verb: him alone, and no other god (verse 35).

decisions.choice: him you shall fear, and to him you shall bow down
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which stresses "him".

decisions.choice: mighty strength
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the outstretched arm (m1).

pieces: Be careful always to keep the statutes and the rulings, the law and the commandment that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote for you, and do not fear other gods.

L.37: And the statutes and the judgments and the law and the commandment that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote for you, you shall be careful to do all the days, and you shall not fear other gods.

R.37: Always be careful to obey the laws and rules, the teaching and the commands that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote down for you. Do not worship other gods.

decisions.choice: which he wrote: Yahweh, spoken of in the third person
decisions.reason: Yahweh is the speaker of verses 35-39 ("I made", verse 38), but here and in verse 36 he is spoken of as "he". The words are a summary of what he commanded rather than an exact quotation.

decisions.choice: which he wrote for you
decisions.reason: Yahweh wrote the commandments on the stone tablets (Exodus 24:12; Deuteronomy 10:4), and the law was written down for Israel at his command (Deuteronomy 31:9).

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments, law, commandment / statutes, rulings, law, commandment / laws, rules, teaching, commands
decisions.reason: As in verse 34.

decisions.choice: do not forget the covenant
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy warns against forgetting the covenant and making idols (Deuteronomy 4:23), and against forgetting Yahweh when the land is full (Deuteronomy 6:12; 8:11).

decisions.choice: I made: Yahweh speaks
decisions.reason: Here the speaker's own voice is heard: the covenant is Yahweh's (verse 37, m1).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

pieces: Fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God instead, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue you from the power of all your enemies."

L.39: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God you shall fear, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."

R.39: Worship only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. He will save you from all your enemies."

decisions.choice: he will deliver you from all your enemies
decisions.reason: The promise stands against what has just happened: Israel sought help from Egypt (verse 4) and fell to Assyria. Fearing Yahweh alone was its only safety (Deuteronomy 20:1-4).

decisions.choice: but only: Yahweh and no other
decisions.reason: As in verse 36, the words set Yahweh against the other gods of verse 38.

decisions.choice: the power of (Balanced); omitted (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power; Readable says simply "from all your enemies".

decisions.reason: The chapter ends as verse 33 did: a worship divided between Yahweh and idols. It passes from parents to children, as Israel's own sin had (verse 14).
